Keystone: Deal._rot_days is keyed on Activity.created_at (row insert time), not on when the contact happened, so year-old deals read 'fresh'

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] HIGH. Deal._rot_days / _rot_level is computed from the created_at (database insert time) of the latest linked Activity, not from when the contact actually happened (due_date of a done activity). Every one of the 177 Activity rows on Keystone has created_at = 2026-09-16 (seed batch), including backdated history such as calls dated Sep 2025. Result: every open deal with any linked activity reads _rot_days = 11 / 'fresh' regardless of true age.

Evidence (read 2026-09-28, GET /api/Deal + GET /api/Activity, 27 open deals):
- Formula _rot_days == days since max(deal.updated_at, latest linked Activity.created_at) matches 27/27 open deals exactly.
- Deal 52f7e986 (stage new): updated_at 2026-08-23 (35 d), only linked activity is a done call due 2025-09-24 -> platform says 11 / fresh.
- Deal bf138f5d (qualification): last done contact 2026-07-13 (77 d), only other activity an OPEN task overdue since 2026-08-22 -> 11 / fresh.
- Deal 019eb426 (negotiation, $266,815): last done contact 2025-10-19 (email), plus one not-done future call -> 11 / fresh.
- By real last-contact date (max of updated_at and due_date of done activities), 8 of 27 open deals are >= 30 days (deal_rot_days = 30). The platform flags 1 (deal 29662773, 38 d, the only open deal with no linked activity).

Impact: the CRM's own 'rotting deals' signal under-reports 8 -> 1 on this book. Any import/backfill of historical activities, or any agent logging a task, resets rot to 0. This is the Keystone form of Suryodaya report 'Creating any linked Activity resets the deal's rot signal' (filed 2026-09-21); on Suryodaya that behaviour no longer reproduced on 2026-09-24, on Keystone it is live, so the two instances also disagree.

Expected: rot should age from the last completed customer contact (done activity's due_date / completed time), ignoring not-done tasks and row insert timestamps.

Keystone: sales-tax exemption (resale certificate) ignored when place_of_supply is set - exempt customer charged $9,699.92 on SO-2026-00003

[Keystone] HIGH (money). Party 'Tri-State Farm Equipment' (e72f519c...) has taxable = 0 and tax_exemption_reason = 'Resale certificate on file (OH ST-1)'. Of its 35 sales documents:
- 31 SalesOrders with place_of_supply = null carry a single line 'Sales tax - exempt (resale certificate)', rate 0, amount 0. Correct.
- 4 documents with place_of_supply = 'OH' are charged full Ohio State Sales Tax 5.75% + Stark County (OH) 0.75%:
  SO-2026-00003  net 149,229.60  tax 9,699.92 (confirmed order)
  QTN-2026-00005 net 149,229.60  tax 9,699.92
  QTN-2026-00006 net  64,467.00  tax 4,190.35
  QTN-2026-00019 net  24,871.60  tax 1,616.66
The split is exact: place_of_supply set -> taxed (4/4); unset -> exempt (31/31). No other taxable=0 party exists to generalise further.

Impact: an exempt reseller is quoted and ordered with 6.5% tax it should not pay (~$25k across the 4 docs). A CRM agent reading these quotes would present wrong totals to the customer.
Repro: GET /api/Party?name=Tri-State Farm Equipment ; GET /api/SalesOrder and /api/Quotation filtered by that party_id; compare taxes[] against party.taxable.
Expected: party.taxable = 0 with an exemption reason should zero tax regardless of place_of_supply.

Keystone: make.orders reports late=false / late_count=0 for 9 of 9 open order lines that are 1-3.5 months past promise; late filter returns nothing

[Keystone] MEDIUM. endpoint.make.orders (GET /api/make/orders), read 2026-09-28, returns 9 rows, late_count 0, every row late: false. All 9 are past their promised date with delivered_qty 0, and the underlying SalesOrders read delivered_status = 'undelivered':
  SO-2026-00003:1 Tri-State Farm Equipment   promised 2026-06-09 qty 1560 delivered 0 late=false
  SO-2026-00002:1 Buckeye AgriPower Inc      promised 2026-07-02 qty 1120 delivered 0 late=false
  SO-2026-00001:1 Cardinal Tillage Works     promised 2026-07-24 qty 2400 delivered 0 late=false
  SO-2026-00006:1, -00008:1, -00004:1 ... promised 2026-08-05 .. 2026-08-26, all 0 delivered, late=false
(promise_basis = 'sales_order_delivery_date', projected = null on every row.)

Secondary: (a) the late filter returns 0 rows (MCP late='true', REST ?late=true), so a 'show me late orders' query answers 'none' for a book where every open line is late; (b) the MCP inputSchema types late as string, not boolean (late=true -> '/late must be string'), while the output field is boolean; (c) any string is accepted, e.g. late='yes' returns 200 unfiltered.

The response does carry source_state = 'incomplete'. That is good disclosure, but when projected is unknown the row should say late = null/unknown or fall back to promised < today - not assert false.
Expected: late = true when promised < today and delivered_qty < qty; late filter typed boolean and validated.

Keystone: Goal progress is wrong - company goals stuck at 0, activity goals disagree with Activity data 12/12, Q4-2026 goals already show progress

[Keystone] MEDIUM. Goal.current_value is inconsistent with the book (100 goals, read 2026-09-28):
1. All 4 company-level 2026 goals (owner 'Keystone Precision Works LLC') read current_value 0.0: revenue (target 8,460,000), deals won (44), new opportunities (96), customer touches (1450). The same book has 23 closed_won deals worth $1,303,083 and 119 done activities dated 2026; the per-rep goals for the same metrics are non-zero. Company goals do not roll up.
2. 'customer touches' (type activities) per-rep goals disagree with Activity (assigned_to = owner, done = 1, due_date in period) on 12 of 12 elapsed goals, e.g. Sheila Rourke Q2 2026: goal 0, activities 14; Ray Kozlowski Q2 2026: goal 0, activities 8.
3. 4 goals for a period that has not started (Q4 2026, start 2026-10-01) already have progress: 'new opportunities' for Sheila Rourke 3, Ray Kozlowski 2, Devon Ashby 7, Dana Whitfield 1.
For contrast, revenue and deals_won per-rep goals match closed_won deals by expected_close_date on 48 of 48, so a rollup exists; it is not applied to company-level goals or to activities/deals_created.
Expected: current_value derived from source records for every goal type, zero for future periods, company goals = rollup.

Keystone: same customer, same ship-to taxed by destination on web orders but by Ohio origin on quote-path orders (place_of_supply=OH for PA/MI addresses)

[Keystone] MEDIUM. Sales-tax sourcing is inconsistent for the same customer and the same (only) address:
- Marcus Webb, ship-to Pittsburgh PA 15222: SO-2026-00164 (web order) charged Pennsylvania 6.0%; SO-2026-00005, QTN-2026-00012, QTN-2026-00018 carry place_of_supply = 'OH' and are charged Ohio 5.75% + Stark County (OH) 0.75%.
- Sam Okafor, ship-to Lansing MI 48911: SO-2026-00166 (web) charged Michigan 6.0%; SO-2026-00007 and QTN-2026-00014 carry place_of_supply = 'OH' and are charged Ohio + Stark County.
Across all 187 quotes/orders, these 5 are the only documents whose taxing state differs from the party's address state; other quote-path documents for PA/MI parties do set place_of_supply to PA/MI.
Caveat: these quotes carry 'FOB North Canton, OH', and origin-vs-destination sourcing depends on state rules, so the tax may be defensible. The defect is that place_of_supply is set to a state that is neither the customer's address nor applied consistently, and the same buyer gets two tax treatments. A pipeline agent quoting totals cannot tell which is right.
Expected: place_of_supply derived from the ship-to address (or explicitly recorded as origin-sourced with a reason), applied consistently per customer.

_rot_level vocabulary differs between instances: Keystone 'warning', Suryodaya 'attention', for the same software and the same deal-rot-config

[Keystone vs Suryodaya] LOW. Same codebase, same GET /api/deal-rot-config -> {default_rot_days: 30, stages: {}} on both, but Deal._rot_level returns different enum values:
- Keystone (class.agentswitch...): fresh 26, warning 1, none 36
- Suryodaya (agentswitch...): fresh 9, attention 81, none 53
_rot_level/_rot_days appear in neither GET /api/Deal/validation-rules nor the Deal.list MCP input/output schema, so there is no contract to code against; a client written on one instance silently counts zero rotting deals on the other if it matches the literal. Related to the Suryodaya report on rot-threshold sources (2026-09-21), which noted the vocabulary was undocumented; the new fact is that it diverges across instances.
Expected: one documented enum, declared in validation-rules and the tool schema.

Keystone: a past call or meeting can never be logged - Activity.due_date may not precede creation, while a DONE activity dated in the future is accepted

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] HIGH. Activity.create and Activity.update reject any due_date earlier than the record's creation date:
  422 deadline_before_creation: 'Due Date cannot be before 2026-09-28, the date this record was created. A deadline that predates the record it belongs to is usually a typo.'
Reproduced 2026-09-28 on both doors (MCP Activity.create/Activity.update, REST POST /api/Activity and PUT /api/Activity/{id}), for done=true and done=false alike, using records created by team07 and tagged [team07-test KS-TP-20260928].

Why it is a bug: for a completed activity (done=true), due_date is the date the call/meeting happened. The most basic CRM action - 'I called them yesterday, log it' - is now impossible; every contact can only be recorded on the day it is entered. Meanwhile the inverse, which is actually impossible, is allowed: done=true with due_date 2026-10-03 and 2026-10-18 (in the future) were both accepted. The rule is inverted for completed activities.

It also contradicts the book: all 177 seeded Keystone activities have created_at 2026-09-16 and due_dates back to 2025-09 (e.g. 'Release schedule check-in - Steve Kowalczyk (Sep 2025)'). Likely side effect (not tested, it needs a write to a record team07 did not create): the 33 open seeded activities whose due_date precedes 2026-09-16 may now be impossible to complete or edit, since any update re-validates due_date.

Impact on rot: the platform ages deals from Activity.created_at (filed earlier today as 'Deal._rot_days is keyed on Activity.created_at'); with this rule, created_at and due_date can never disagree for new rows, but the seeded history already does.
Expected: for done activities, allow past dates and reject future ones; apply the 'deadline' rule only to open tasks, if at all.

Keystone: Deal.create accepts any stage string, and a deal created in an invalid stage can never be closed

[Keystone] HIGH. Deal.create validates `pipeline` (a nonexistent pipeline -> 'Referenced Pipeline does not exist in this workspace') but not `stage`:
- stage 'negotiation' on pipeline 'jigs' (whose stages are new/qualification/closed_won/closed_lost) -> accepted (deal c381387e).
- stage 'bogus_stage' on pipeline 'new_business' -> accepted (deal 53ddc47a-...).
The state machine is enforced everywhere else: Deal.update refuses state fields ('State fields [stage] cannot be changed via PUT. Use POST /api/Deal/{id}/transition instead.').

Consequence: the bogus_stage deal can never leave that state. POST /api/Deal/53ddc47a.../transition -> 400 "Invalid current state 'bogus_stage' for flow 'DealFlow'. Valid states: ['new','qualification','proposal','negotiation','closed_won','closed_lost']"; no Deal.mark_lost.* tool exists for it; PUT refuses the stage. The record is stuck open in the shared book.

Cleanup request: deal 53ddc47a titled '[team07-test KS-TP-20260928] V-bogus-stage' (value 0, party '[team07-test KS-TP-20260928] P7-value-rollup') is a team07 test fixture created to demonstrate this bug. It cannot be closed by any seat tool - please close or delete it. Until then it puts a test party into every Keystone CRM team's pipeline and 'not called' views.
Expected: Deal.create validates stage against the deal's pipeline stages (and the DealFlow states), exactly as the transition endpoint does.

Keystone: Activity.create accepts a deal_id and party_id that belong to different customers

[Keystone] MEDIUM. Activity.create accepted an activity with deal_id = a deal whose party is customer P1 and party_id = a different customer P2 (both team07 fixtures, tagged [team07-test KS-TP-20260928], activity subject '... V-deal-party-mismatch'). Nothing checks that the activity's party is the deal's party.

Impact: every per-customer contact view now counts one activity for two customers - the deal's history says P1 was contacted, the party's history says P2 was. Agents and reports that link contact by party (necessary on Keystone, where 86 of 177 activities have no deal_id) attribute contact to the wrong customer.
Expected: when both are given, reject a party_id that differs from the deal's party_id (or derive party_id from the deal).

Keystone: a deal created without a pipeline is silently filed under 'oem' although no default pipeline is configured

[Keystone] LOW. Deal.create with no `pipeline` argument produced a deal with pipeline = 'oem' (deal 3d7234b9, team07 fixture). CRMPreferences.default_deal_pipeline is null, so nothing configured says 'oem' is the default, and the Deal.create schema declares no default for pipeline. Either the default should be configured and visible (CRMPreferences), or the field should stay empty / be required.
Expected: a documented default, or none.

Keystone: a won deal's value can be rewritten after close, even to 0 - the 'won deals must have value > 0' rule is enforced only on create

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM. Deal.create rejects a closed_won deal with value 0 ('Won deals must have a value greater than zero'). Deal.update does not re-check it: on team07 fixture deal 2b460a14 ('[team07-test KS-BH-20260928] BH-deal', closed_won - terminal), Deal.update {value: 1} and then {value: 0} were both accepted; the deal now reads closed_won with value 0.0. Reproduced 2026-09-28 via MCP Deal.update.

Why it matters: closed_won is terminal ('From closed_won you can go to: nowhere'), so its value is booked revenue. It can be silently rewritten afterwards - to any amount, including one the create path forbids - with nothing but updated_at to show for it. Revenue goals (current_value for revenue/deals_won goals) and any won-value report are computed from these rows.

Note on the fixture: this deal reached closed_won by accident during team07 negative testing (Deal.mark_won.qualification.closed_won is a legitimate edge; the probe was mistaken for a negative case). It has no owner and no expected_close_date, and its value was then set to 0 using this very bug so it adds nothing to won-value totals. It cannot be closed_lost or deleted from this seat - please remove it if you prefer it gone.
Expected: value (and other revenue fields) read-only once a deal is terminal, or at minimum the won-value > 0 rule enforced on update as on create.

Keystone: Activity accepts negative duration, an impossible due_time (25:99) and due_date 9999-12-31

[Keystone] LOW-MEDIUM. Activity.create (MCP) accepted, on team07 fixtures tagged [team07-test KS-BH-20260928]:
- duration: -30  (stored -30.0)
- due_time: '25:99' (stored verbatim)
- due_date: '9999-12-31'
The same endpoint rejects '2026-02-30' and '28/09/2026' as invalid dates, and (PB1, report 80aa56f5) rejects any due_date before the record's creation - so the date check exists but has no upper bound, and due_time/duration are not validated at all.
Impact: calendar/reminder views (enable_activity_reminders=1, reminder_before_hours=1.0) and any duration totals receive values that cannot be scheduled or summed.
Expected: duration >= 0; due_time a valid HH:MM (00:00-23:59); a sane upper bound on due_date.

Keystone: Deal.currency accepts any string ('XYZ') and a currency the company does not use ('INR' in a USD-only book)

[Keystone] LOW-MEDIUM. Deal.create accepted currency 'XYZ' (not an ISO 4217 code) and currency 'INR' on Keystone Precision Works LLC, whose CRMPreferences.default_currency is USD and whose 63 seeded deals are all USD (team07 fixtures D-currency-bogus / D-currency-INR, tagged [team07-test KS-BH-20260928], value 0, since closed_lost).
Deals carry _base_value/_base_currency for conversion; a non-ISO code has no rate, and an INR deal in a US GAAP / Sales & Use Tax book is a locale error (the Suryodaya-vs-Keystone split is exactly this). Pipeline value and forecast sums mix or drop such rows silently.
Expected: currency validated against ISO 4217, and against the company's enabled currencies (or explicitly converted).

Keystone: inconsistent date rules - a new deal may have expected_close_date in the past, while a past Activity date is refused; lost_reason accepted on an open deal

[Keystone] LOW. (1) Deal.create accepted expected_close_date 2020-01-01 on a brand-new deal in stage 'new' (team07 fixture D-close-date-past). The platform refuses a past due_date on any Activity (PB1, report 80aa56f5, 'a deadline that predates the record ... is usually a typo'), but applies no such rule to the deal's own close date - the one date that drives forecasting and 'past expected close' views. The two rules are inverted relative to each other.
(2) Deal.create accepted lost_reason on a deal created in stage 'qualification' (fixture D-lost-reason-on-open); lost_reason should only be meaningful on closed_lost.
Both fixtures are tagged [team07-test KS-BH-20260928] and now closed_lost.
Expected: one consistent date policy (warn or refuse past expected_close_date on open deals, allow past dates for completed activities); lost_reason only with closed_lost.

[Keystone, US tenant] MEDIUM. Read-only MCP audit on 2026-09-28 found nine converted Quotation -> SalesOrder pairs. In all nine, the source Quotation has currency_code = USD, while the linked SalesOrder detail has no currency or currency_code field. The SalesOrder.list tool contract also has no currency_code field. Party, place_of_supply, net_total, total_tax, and grand_total match in all nine pairs, isolating the defect to currency preservation/serialization.

Impact: an order API consumer cannot determine whether monetary totals are USD from the order itself after quote conversion, risking incorrect display, export, integration, or audit handling.

Repro (read-only): tools/list; Quotation.list(limit=1000); SalesOrder.list(limit=1000); choose a SalesOrder with quotation_id; call Quotation.get(source id) and SalesOrder.get(order id). Observe currency_code=USD on the quotation and no currency field on the order.

Expected: a converted SalesOrder retains and serializes the source currency_code=USD, and the SalesOrder contract declares it.

[Keystone, US tenant] LOW API-contract/localization defect. Read-only MCP tools/list and entity get responses on 2026-09-28 expose gst_no, gst_treatment, and is_reverse_charge for Quotation and SalesOrder. Keystone is configured as a US customer book with USD default currency and US sales-tax rules. The observed values were null/0; this report does not claim that tax was calculated incorrectly.

Impact: a US-facing Pipeline consumer is offered India-specific operational tax vocabulary and can build invalid or misleading workflows instead of using the tenant's US sales-tax model. This makes the tenant contract ambiguous and increases integration error risk.

Repro (read-only): call tools/list and inspect Quotation.list/SalesOrder.list input schemas; call Quotation.get or SalesOrder.get for an existing USD record. gst_no, gst_treatment, and is_reverse_charge are exposed.

Expected: U.S. tenant API contracts surface only applicable U.S. tax fields. If a shared internal schema must remain, the India-specific fields should be suppressed or clearly non-operational in the U.S. external contract.

Keystone: sales tax is computed from the client-supplied line 'amount' before the server recomputes it - a $100 order is charged $5,750 tax

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] HIGH (money). Quotation.create and SalesOrder.create accept an optional items[].amount. The server correctly overwrites the line amount with qty x rate, but the sales-tax engine has already run on the client's value.

Reproduced 2026-09-29 via MCP on team07 fixtures (customer '[team07-test KS-BH-20260929] cust-OH', billing Canton OH, FG-TIL-2200):
- QTN-2026-00025: qty 1, rate 100, amount 100000 -> stored line amount 100.00, net_total 100.00, total_tax 5750.00 (5.75% of 100000), grand_total 5850.00. Tax is 57.5x the net.
- SO-2026-00171: same payload on SalesOrder.create -> net 100.00, tax 5750.00.
- QTN-2026-00022: qty 10, rate 125.2, amount 1 -> net 1252.00, tax 0.06 (expected 71.99).
- QTN-2026-00024: amount 0 -> tax 719.90, correct (0 appears to be treated as 'not supplied').
- QTN-2026-00021 (no amount) -> tax 71.99, correct.

The two paths disagree: when the client sends a wrong taxes[] row instead, create is refused with 'Taxes do not match the computed tax: expected 71.99 on 1252.00 at 5.75%, got 0.01' - so the validator uses the recomputed net, but the engine that writes taxes[] uses the raw client amount.

Impact: any API/MCP client (including agents) can under-collect sales tax to near zero or over-charge a customer, and the document still looks internally consistent line by line.
Expected: compute tax only from the server-recomputed line amounts (or reject a client amount that differs from qty x rate x (1-discount)).

Keystone: approval can be self-granted - approval_status 'approved' is accepted on Quotation.create / SalesOrder.create although only admin/finance_admin may approve

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] HIGH (separation of duties). The platform states the rule itself: POST /api/Quotation/{id}/approve from seat team07 (role sales_user) returns 403 'Only an approver (admin or finance_admin) can approve this document. Submitting it for approval is the creator's step; the decision belongs to someone else.' Quotation.update {approval_status: 'approved'} is likewise refused ('Permission denied').

But create does not enforce it. Reproduced 2026-09-29 via MCP on team07 fixtures:
- Quotation.create {..., approval_status: 'approved'} -> QTN-2026-00023 stored with approval_status 'approved'.
- SalesOrder.create {..., approval_status: 'approved'} -> SO-2026-00168 stored with approval_status 'approved'.
(Contrast: status is protected on create - 'Quotation.status is a state machine and cannot be set on create'.)

Expected: approval_status must be server-owned on create (always 'not_required' or computed from approval rules), exactly as status is.

Keystone: a quotation that is pending approval can be sent to the customer

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM. Reproduced 2026-09-29 on team07 fixture QTN-2026-00032: Quotation.create (approval_status not_required) -> Quotation.approval.submit -> approval_status 'pending_approval' -> Quotation.send -> status 'sent' while approval_status is still 'pending_approval'. No approver ever acted. (The fixture has since been declined.)

Submitting for approval therefore has no effect on what the creator can do next; the price/terms under review reach the customer before the decision.
Expected: the draft->sent transition (and SalesOrder draft->confirmed) should be refused while approval_status is pending_approval or rejected.

Notification.list returns every user's in-app notifications, including content from apps the caller is denied (contracts, approvals, engineering)

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] HIGH (cross-user and cross-app disclosure). Seat team07 (role sales_user, allowed_apps ['crm','agent'], user id 443778c5) reads 122 Notification rows via REST GET /api/Notification and MCP Notification.list. None is addressed to team07: recipients are 7 other user ids, the roles 'admin' and 'manufacturing_user', and 33 with no recipient.

The messages carry content from apps this seat is refused: entity_type ContractObligation (15), Contract (1), ApprovalRequest (37), DesignFile/DesignFeedback/DesignReview (38), EngineeringChangeOrder (1). Examples: "Obligation 'Pin condition audit before refresh - Buckeye AgriPower Inc' is now OVERDUE"; "Contract 'Vendor Agreement - sheet and bar - Apex Metals Supply LLC' ... has expired"; "ECO ECO-2026-00004 approved: ...". Meanwhile GET /api/ContractObligation and /api/Contract return 403 "App 'contracts' is not enabled for your account". The MCP rows also carry _entity_id_display, which resolves the name of the 403'd record.

Same on Suryodaya (team07): 1233 notifications, 743 with no recipient, 86 to 'admin', the rest to other users; entity types include AgentJob, ContractObligation, DesignReview, ContractDocument.

Expected: Notification reads are scoped to recipient = caller (or a role the caller holds), and display resolution respects the target entity's app gate.

Relation to earlier report B1 (8212c63a, Suryodaya, 'app-entitlement gate enforced on entity routes but NOT on composite app routes'): same family, different hole. B1 covers purpose-built routes (/api/manufacturing/demand-forecast etc.). This one is a core ENTITY route (Notification) that carries other apps' content, and it also returns rows addressed to OTHER USERS, which B1 does not cover. Fixing B1's composite routes would not fix this.

Keystone: line items of any engine-taxed Quotation/SalesOrder cannot be edited - the server rejects its own stored tax row

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM. When the US tax engine computes tax it stores a 15-field taxes[] row (tax_regime, jurisdiction_id, jurisdiction_name, jurisdiction_level, state_code, county, city, sourcing, liability_account_id, is_exempt, exemption_certificate_id, rate_source plus tax_type/rate/amount). Any later update that touches items re-validates that stored row against the 3-column schema and fails.

Reproduced 2026-09-29 on team07 fixture QTN-2026-00021: Quotation.update {id, items:[same line]} and {items:[qty 11]} both fail: "Taxes row 1: unknown fields 'city', 'county', 'exemption_certificate_id', 'is_exempt', 'jurisdiction_id', ... Valid columns are: amount, rate, ...". REST PUT /api/Quotation/{id} -> 422 same message. Sending taxes: [] still fails. SalesOrder.update {items} on SO-2026-00169 fails the same way. Updates that don't touch items (notes, valid_till) succeed.

Only workaround: resend taxes[] with the 3 base columns - which is accepted, but the stored row loses jurisdiction_id, liability_account_id, sourcing etc., i.e. the edit silently strips the data that ties the tax to its GL liability account.
Expected: the update validator accepts the server's own tax row shape (or recomputes tax and ignores stored rows).

Keystone: Lead -> Deal chain is unguarded - make.Deal works on a disqualified lead, repeats without limit, and duplicates the deal Lead.convert already created

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM. Reproduced 2026-09-29 on team07 fixture leads (party '[team07-test KS-BH-20260929] cust-OH'):
1. Lead a16e88bc: Lead.disqualify -> 'disqualified'; Lead.make.Deal -> creates open Deal 430c2e5c (stage new, value 1000).
2. Lead 14fadcc2 (status new): Lead.make.Deal twice -> two open deals (c74a44b1, d1a1279f), both lead_id = the lead; the lead stays 'new'.
3. Lead aab88a7b: contact -> qualify -> convert. With CRMPreferences.auto_create_deal_on_lead_convert = 1, convert auto-creates Deal 510fd3e0 titled 'Deal from f17e675a-27a0-4b12-b860-6bac8a32101a' (the party's UUID although the party has a name). Lead.make.Deal afterwards creates a second deal bd5eb648 for the same converted lead.
(All five fixture deals have been closed_lost.)

Note: the 'Deal from <uuid>' title is the same defect as Suryodaya report B4; the 2026-09-28 Keystone hunt recorded it as absent because no seeded deal used this path - it is present in Keystone's code.
Impact: duplicate pipeline value, deals for leads marked not-a-fit, and lead status that never reflects conversion.
Expected: make.Deal refused for disqualified/converted leads (or idempotent per lead), and moving the lead to converted; auto-created deal titled from the party name.

Keystone: US vendor tax profile (W-9 / 1099 / backup withholding) has no cross-field validation - a 1099 vendor with no W-9 is not backup-withheld

[Keystone, class.agentswitch.theschoolofai.in] MEDIUM (US compliance). _rot_level: "none" — 49 deals, which is exactly the set of closed deals (29 closed_lost + 20 closed_won)

Publish the _rot_level enum and the exact rule mapping _rot_days → level. If attention is an intentional mid-band (e.g. "past half the threshold"), say so — at default_rot_days: 14, a band starting at 7 would explain the 8-day observations, but that is our inference, not documentation.

Controlled single-record test on 2026-09-21:

Before	After
Deal 7de1dd77-e95d-490c-978e-bd8f2064a4b5	_rot_level: attention, _rot_days: 8	_rot_level: fresh, _rot_days: 0

Critically, the activity that reset the signal was:

So _rot_days appears to measure "days since an activity was attached to this deal", not days in stage and not days since actual contact. That also explains Bug 1's uniform 8-day cohort: 81 deals had no linked activity at all, so all of them measured from the same seed point.

Why it's a real bug

This is a feedback loop, and it is dangerous specifically because the platform is agent-oriented.

Merely intending to act marks a deal healthy. Scheduling a follow-up for next week — or simply logging that someone ought to call — moves the deal from attention to fresh immediately, before anyone speaks to the customer.
Any automated agent that writes next actions will launder its own pipeline. The seat's canonical task ends in "…and what is the next action on each", i.e. writing an Activity per rotting deal. Doing that to all 81 deals would return the entire rotting pipeline to fresh in one pass, having contacted nobody. The next scheduled run would then find nothing wrong. A genuinely neglected deal becomes invisible precisely because it was flagged.
The metric is trivially gameable, including unintentionally, by any rep who bulk-creates tasks.
We stopped after one deal for this reason and left the other 18 untouched.

What would resolve it

Compute rot from something an agent's own bookkeeping cannot fake. Options, in rough order of preference:

Count only completed activities (done: true) — a real touchpoint, not an intention.
Ignore activities dated in the future.
Key rot off stage-entry date instead (days in current stage), which is what "rotting" usually means in a pipeline and what the existing _rot_days naming implies.
Exclude agent-authored rows from the calculation.
Related: Activity._permissions.delete is false for this seat, so an agent can create rows affecting the rot metric but cannot remove them. Cleanup of the one row we created needs an account with delete rights.

the change was intentional and additive.

result; (3) move serverInfo.version when the surface changes; (4) document whether

B5-ADDENDUM — `done` is boolean-on-input but integer-on-output: a record's own value cannot be fed back into a filter

Addendum to report 83f4db3d-bb21-4766-b0eb-a24a7246bd13 (validation-rules declares
bool, API returns int). That report called it a type-fidelity mismatch. Testing the
write path today showed it is stronger than that: it is a round-trip failure.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED (2026-09-24, MCP entity-scoped surface)

Reading an Activity returns `done` as an integer:

  GET /api/Activity  ->  "done": 0        (160 rows)   /   "done": 1   (16 rows)

Filtering Activity.list by that same field REQUIRES a JSON boolean:

  Activity.list {"deal_id": "<id>", "done": false}  ->  200, total=1
  Activity.list {"deal_id": "<id>", "done": 0}      ->  -32602
      {"code":"invalid_arguments",
       "errors":[{"field":"/done","message":"/done must be boolean."}]}

So the value the API hands you for `done` is precisely the value the API refuses when
you hand it back.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A COSMETIC MISMATCH

A client that reads a row, takes `row["done"]`, and uses it to search for similar rows
gets a hard error. The natural, correct-looking code is the code that breaks. Ours
happens to send a Python `False` literal rather than the value it read, so it works by
luck rather than by design - and that luck is invisible in the source.

It also means `validation-rules` is wrong in a specific, actionable way rather than a
vague one: for `done` it should say the write/filter type is boolean, whatever the read
representation is.

SUGGESTED FIX

Accept both 0/1 and true/false on input, or return JSON booleans on output. Either
direction makes read-then-filter work; the current split makes it a trap.

Severity: Low/Medium. No data is wrong; the API contract is not round-trippable.

Malformed Pipeline stage records — elaborated
What was observed: Suryodaya's Pipeline entity (company id starting 5cbe5a55… — full id not captured in this conversation, needs re-fetching before filing) returned 6 records. Two are well-formed sales pipelines: - OEM New Business (oem_new_business): Enquiry → RFQ/Feasibility → Quotation Sent → Commercial Negotiation → Nomination Won/Lost - SuryaTools Trade Channel (suryatools_trade_channel): Enquiry → Samples Sent → Price List Shared → Terms → Dealer Signed/Lost
The other 4 are not sales pipelines at all — names and "stages" are manufacturing/inventory artifacts, not sales-stage vocabulary: - Lathe Dog 47mm (Kg) - Bench Vice 30mm (Kg) - Punch Set 142mm (Nos) - Tap Wrench 158mm (Kg)
Why it's a real bug, not cosmetic: Pipeline.stages defines the state machine every Deal moves through. Any deal attached to one of these 4 malformed pipelines has a corrupted, unusable state machine — directly undermines the seat's core graded task, since "which deals are rotting" depends on reading meaningful stage transitions.
Strong root-cause lead, already present in the data: the Pipeline schema itself carries a comment describing exactly this failure mode — "key-less pipelines and deals storing a display name instead of a key." That's the schema author documenting a known bug pattern, suggesting an unfixed data-import/migration issue where product/inventory SKU names leaked into the pipeline-definition table instead of proper sales-stage keys.
For the report: include the 4 malformed record names, the company id, note that 2 of 6 records are correctly formed (rules out "the feature is entirely broken" — it's specifically these 4 rows), and quote the schema's own comment as corroborating evidence this is a known, named failure mode rather than a one-off.
